---
title: "PBLUP — Pedigree-Based BLUP"
---

PBLUP is the classical animal model: genetic similarity is measured
entirely from pedigree records, without any genotype data required.

$$
\mathbf{K} = \mathbf{A},
$$

where **A** is the **numerator relationship matrix** (NRM). Entry
$A_{ij} = 2\phi_{ij}$ (twice the kinship coefficient); diagonal
$A_{ii} = 1 + F_i$ where $F_i$ is the pedigree inbreeding
coefficient. The full derivation of **A** via Wright's path-counting
algorithm is in
[Biallelic & Multi-allelic](biallelic-and-multiallelic.qmd#eq-a-matrix).

## Biological Intuition

**A** captures *expected* allele sharing identical by descent (IBD):
a parent–offspring pair is expected to share 50 % of their alleles
IBD, full-sibs 50 %, half-sibs 25 %. These are expectations —
averages over random Mendelian segregation — not measurements of
what actually happened.

Two full-sibs that by chance inherited mostly the same chromosomes
will have $A_{ij} = 0.5$, the same as two full-sibs that inherited
mostly different chromosomes. PBLUP cannot distinguish these cases;
GBLUP can, because it observes the actual alleles each animal carries.

## Key Assumptions

- Pedigree records are complete and accurately assigned to each
  individual.
- All relevant relatives are recorded — cryptic relationships outside
  the pedigree (e.g. misassigned parentage, unrecorded relatives)
  inflate residual variance and bias $\hat{\mathbf{u}}$.

::: {.callout-note}
Whenever genotype data are available, GBLUP or GBLUP with microhaplotypes is preferred
over PBLUP. Genotype-based methods use *realised* allele sharing
rather than *expected* sharing, which captures the Mendelian sampling
deviation of each individual within its family.
:::

## See it in Code

```{r}
#| eval: false
library(masreml)

d <- load_data("large")
y <- d$pheno$y_cont_qtl_snp
names(y) <- d$pheno$id
X_fixed <- stats::model.matrix(~ sex, data = d$pheno)

# Build A from pedigree integer IDs
ped_int <- data.frame(
  id   = d$pedigree$id,
  sire = ifelse(is.na(d$pedigree$sire), 0L,
                match(d$pedigree$sire, d$pedigree$id)),
  dam  = ifelse(is.na(d$pedigree$dam),  0L,
                match(d$pedigree$dam,  d$pedigree$id))
)
A_full  <- build_A_ped(ped_int)

# Subset to phenotyped animals only — MME operates on this submatrix
A_pheno <- A_full[d$pheno$id, d$pheno$id]

fit_pblup <- masreml(
  y     = y,
  X     = X_fixed,
  G     = list(snp_add = A_pheno),
  trait = "continuous"
)
summary(fit_pblup)
```
